evidence.note: After orientation, the agent forms a flat numbered task list ('1) exec_numeric, 2) Call/CallIndirect, 3) SIMD decode, 4) SIMD execution, 5) v128 helpers'). This is a two-phase MVP-then-SIMD idea but with no dependency-aware ordering and no per-family done criteria — an undifferentiated punch list.

SIMD is conceptually grouped by shape (i8x16, i16x8, i32x4, i64x2, f32x4, f64x2, narrowing/widening, conversions, dot, Q15), and simd_const.json is re-run as a rough checkpoint — but the approach is to regenerate the entire runtime.rs monolithically rather than implement and verify family by family against distinct spec_json files.

At 21.5% the agent restates the same coarse three-bucket list ('validate_module, SIMD operations, MVP bugs') repeatedly across steps — planning language is recycled verbatim with no evolving milestone hierarchy or per-family exit checks; the same flat list persists rather than being refined.

Late trajectory shows continued whole-file regeneration ('write complete runtime.rs'), backup corruption, and restores. exec_simd ends with only i8x16/i16x8 shapes done; families were never sequenced as ordered milestones each bound to a spec test — the work stayed one big push. No TodoWrite ever used across 230 steps.

reasoning: The agent has a genuine two-phase notion (fix MVP, then add SIMD) and does enumerate the SIMD shape families and occasionally run individual spec files (i32.json, block.json, simd_const.json) as rough checkpoints — putting it above anchor 0. But it never operationalizes a family-by-family implementation with each family's matching spec_json as its done-check (anchor 5); instead it repeatedly regenerates the entire runtime.rs monolithically, recycles the same flat three-bucket task list, and thrashes on file corruption/restores. This matches anchor 3 ('vague two-phase idea with no sub-structure and no per-family done criteria') with only slight lean toward 5 due to the shape enumeration.
